figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of the proposed HiMatch-AD framework. Our HiMatch-AD framework contains two steps: K support images are retrieved through dual-branch matching (left). Then the query and support images are sent to the hierarchical training-free anomaly detection pipeline for anomaly map generation (upper right). The details of A-Map Gen module are shown on the bottom right. Here “Enc.” denotes the encoder, where DINOv3 is applied.
Table 1. Comparisons to SOTA models on BMAD benchmark datasets. The best results are in bold and the second best are underlined.

Fig. 2. Quantitative comparison of different ViT backbones for feature extraction (left). Performance and inference speed as the number of support images K increases from 1 to 16 (middle). Visualization of anomaly maps generated by our approach, with green contours indicating anomalous regions (right).
Table 2. Ablation studies of the matching method and the fusion method of our proposed method HiMatch-AD. We keep the number of the support set K to 4 across all ablation experiments.
